messages:
Maria Gomez: FYI customer X reported sudden p99 spikes on redwood-xl-7b after yesterday's runtime build (build-2024-04-14). p95 up ~25%, p99 up ~2x for short generation. Repro attached below.
Sanjay Patel: I see it in metrics — the kernel selector is failing over to SDPA (software) on several hosts. Quick log from selector: 
```
[2024-04-14T22:03:12Z] kernel_selector: try FlashAttention kernel (BLOCK=128)
[2024-04-14T22:03:12Z] kernel_selector: FlashAttention verify failed: dtype int8 not supported on sm=86
[2024-04-14T22:03:12Z] kernel_selector: fallback -> SDPA_general (slow path)
```
Alex Li: repro steps I used (short prompt, single request):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-7b","input":"Summarize: foo","max_tokens":32}'
```
Results: tail latency spikes to ~2-3x baseline, and launcher logs show flash kernels skipped.
infra-bot: deploy: runtime/build-2024-04-14-37 promoted to prod :package: (canary -> prod)
Maria Gomez: Quick smoke: I toggled FLASH_ATTENTION=0 on one node-pool; p99 dropped back to expected within ~90s but throughput dropped and CPU increased ~10-18%. Tradeoff.
Sanjay Patel: Root cause summary from kernel team: a compile-time change enabled -DUSE_FAST_SDPA, which introduced new FlashAttention kernels that are faster but require stricter GPU/driver combo (BLOCK_SIZE=128 and specific int8 support). Hosts with older drivers (<=520) or different SM fall back to SDPA. Previously we had broader compatibility.
oncall-bot: @oncall-pager notified (page sent)
Alex Li: Short-term mitigation proposal:
- rollback the fast-sdpa flag on canary (rebuild with -DUSE_FAST_SDPA=0)
- expose runtime toggle RUNTIME_FLASHATTN=auto|on|off for emergency hotfixes
- alert/metric kernel_fallback_count to detect early regressions
Sanjay Patel: Also adding a driver-compat check to kernel selector: validate driver version and compute capability before choosing a Flash kernel. Will add unit tests for driver matrix (515/520/525/530).
Maria Gomez: I've opened ticket RD-12345 with repro curl, kernel_selector logs, and perf graphs. Linking customer ticket.
support-bot: customer ticket C-9876 updated with temporary workaround and ETA for rollback.
Alex Li: For Private customers we can give config snippet as workaround: 
```
# runtime.yaml
runtime:
  flash_attention: false
  sdpa_mode: legacy
```
Maria Gomez: Communicate tradeoffs: disabling flash lowers cost-efficiency but avoids high p99. We should offer clear guidance in the support reply.
Sanjay Patel: Long-term: change selector to be conservative; only opt-in to fast kernels when full compatibility is confirmed. Also consider compiling multiple block-size variants (64/128) to widen compatibility but note perf tradeoffs.
Alex Li: I'll own the runtime toggle + customer config docs. Sanjay will own selector compatibility checks + CI matrix. Maria will coordinate customer comms and the rollback schedule.
Maria Gomez: Action timeline: rollback canary build now, monitor p95/p99 for 1 hour, then promote. Short-term add toggle to console in 24-48h. Mid-term expand CI and safe-kernel-selection logic.
Sanjay Patel: Added test plan: run kernel selector unit tests against container images with nvidia-driver {515,520,525,535} and CUDA compat layers to assert no fallback for supported configs.
Maria Gomez: Will post updates here as we progress; thanks all. :raised_hands:
